scope: Native-only structural damage experiment on real papers/slides and generated direct-TikZ pages; not end-to-end or presentation latency.

methodology.percentile: nearest rank p95; six measured samples per edit group, so p95 is the maximum
methodology.estimatedExport: analysis + render (baseline: png-draw) + png-color + png-compare + png-encode + text-bounds; excludes oracle/full-reference work, compiler, display-list construction, IPC and webview
methodology.direct: Per-cell temporary pixmap avoidance; no imported-PDF fingerprint cache in this experiment.
methodology.savings: Paired baseline minus direct export milliseconds; positive saves time. Speedups are baseline/direct ratios.
methodology.hindsight: min(baseline, direct), an unattainable selection bound with exact future costs and maintained signature base.
methodology.hindsightWithSunkAnalysis: min(baseline + direct analysis, direct): shows that analysis is already paid if fallback is decided after damage analysis. Still an optimistic, non-deployable bound.
methodology.gateReplay: OFFLINE counterfactual, not a native implementation. Repeat0 calibrates baseline png-draw and discards signature base. Later choose full when last observed full draw <= threshold or every16th sample; full discards signature base. Otherwise cold costs baseline export + direct analysis, re-establishes base and observes baseline png-draw; warm costs direct export and retains base. Warm all-cell redraw observes direct render as approximate full paint (including clone/clear overhead). Selection uses prior observations only; no oracle/reference timing.
methodology.gateReplayLimits: Warmups train state but do not enter cost summaries. Seven-edit sequences are short; repeated calibration and cold-start cost are paid. Replay does not measure native policy overhead, signature memory, presentation or revision age; separate-run timings are counterfactual estimates.

policyLimitations: These measurements determine whether gains occur on the sampled workloads; they do not establish a universally beneficial damage path.
A per-frame minimum requires knowing both rendering costs before choosing and is not an implementable policy.
Bypassing damage analysis invalidates the signature base for subsequent revisions; a policy needs cheap probes, signature maintenance/rebuild costs, or partial feedback.
Oracle verification work is excluded from sums but perturbs CPU and cache behavior. Six samples, one machine, fixed viewport and zoom.
Pixel equality on sampled edits is not a correctness proof for arbitrary clipping, transparency, masks, moved content or resources.
No presentation latency, revision age, scrolling, peak memory or general user workload distribution is measured.
